text:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy started for model "rwd-model-v3" weightset "w_v3_20260316" -> 2% traffic. tag: canary

jess: seeing weird tokenization/parse errors against canary in metrics dashboard — spike in "unknown token id" logs and tokenization exceptions.

kevin: I’m paged in. Oncall. Can you paste a sample log line?

jess: sample: `ERROR tokenizer: unknown_token_id=50234 seq_id=1245 request_id=abc-123` — happening on 3 hosts in us-west-2 canary pool.

nina: quick grep shows those hosts have tokenizer artifact v2.1 while weightset expects vocab v3.0 — looks like tokenizer config drift.

ops-oncall: paging all — @kevin taking lead. Potential customer visible garbled outputs. Reducing canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary traffic reduced -> 0.7% (automated) per ops-oncall request.

kevin: Confirming routing map: alias "model:rwd:v3" points to weightset w_v3_20260316 but some routing shards are resolving to an older image due to a stale shardmap refresh. Ambiguous routing observed.

jess: I can reproduce locally by forcing mixed tokenizer + new weights — outputs are garbled, tokens mismatch.

support-bot: Customer impact: 7 support tickets opened in last 12m mentioning garbled completions; no auth errors or data leakage reported. Severity: P2->escalating to P1 until rollback.

product-cto: Notifying Sales/CS for top-customers on affected routes. Drafting short status note.

kevin: Immediate plan: 1) Flip rollout flag to stop routing to v3 canary 2) Promote stable alias back to w_v2 3) Evacuate canary hosts and reprovision images with pinned tokenizer artifact.

jess: flag name is `serve_v3_weights` — ready to flip if ops approves.

ops-oncall: Approved. Flipping flag now.

jess: command: ```curl -XPOST https://flags.internal/flip -d 'flag=serve_v3_weights&value=false'```

deploy-bot: Feature flag "serve_v3_weights" set to false by ops-oncall. Traffic fallback to stable.

kevin: Running weightset alias rollback: `weight-alias set model=rwd stable=w_v2_20260228`

deploy-bot: Alias update acknowledged. Routing convergence in progress (expect ~20s).

nina: Evacuating the 3 offending canary hosts and queuing a golden image bake with tokenizer v3 pinned.

jess: Monitoring logs — token errors dropping. Metric: token_error_rate was 1.8% at peak, down to 0.03% after rollback.

support-bot: Customer impact update: new tickets continue to come but automated responses sent. CS queued targeted emails for the 3 customers who reported corrupt outputs.

kevin: Confirmed rollback complete, canary traffic now 0%. No further tokenizer-exception traces in last 5m.

product-cto: Great — please prepare a short postmortem and TTRETA for customers.

ops-oncall: Filing incident INC-20260316-01 and assigning to eng-runtime for follow-up (postmortem, RCAs, pipeline validation).

nina: Root cause summary: image bake pipeline omitted pinned tokenizer artifact hash for this release. Some rolling nodes picked older tokenizer artifact due to race in shardmap refresh. Will add strict artifact pinning + pre-deploy validation to pipeline and a guard to abort canary if token_error_rate > 0.5%.

kevin: Also adding a routing consistency check: require alias resolution consistency across all routing shards before opening canary traffic above 1%.

jess: I'll collect sample traces and run a regression test suite before we attempt another canary.

ops-oncall: Status: mitigated -> rollback complete. Assign follow-ups and schedule postmortem.

product-cto: Thanks team. Follow-up items: communication to affected customers, deploy-pipeline patch, routing-consistency gate, and adding automated canary-abort on token errors.

jess: Closing thread for now. Will update once postmortem is attached. :white_check_mark:
